figures.caption: Precedence and unary negation produce the value 24 from the seventeen-byte input.
figures.alt: Four annotated details at expression return for 18 - 3 * (2 + -4). Native signed status is zero and result is 24. The unchanged seventeen-byte input begins at 0x10010004 after its guard and spans two memory rows. A separate caller-memory row shows length seventeen and both result words still 99 before publication.

figures.caption: A missing closing parenthesis is reported before division can use the grouped denominator.
figures.alt: Four annotated details for the six-byte input 1/(2-2. Native status is minus one and byte offset six. The group has no closing parenthesis, although its subtraction yields zero. The input ends at offset six before the mapped zero padding; no byte at that end position is read. Caller memory retains status and result 99.

figures.caption: The positive decimal literal overflows before its preceding unary minus can be applied.
figures.alt: Four annotated details for -2147483648. Native status is minus two and error offset ten. The final digit eight at address 0x1001000e makes the positive literal exceed 2147483647 before unary negation. Length is eleven and both caller result words remain 99. Input and all neighboring data are unchanged.

figures.caption: A complete group returns zero, so division reports its operator at byte one.
figures.alt: Four annotated details for the seven-byte input 1/(2-2). Native status is minus three and error offset one. The group closes successfully and supplies denominator zero. The slash at address 0x10010005 is the reported operator byte. The caller-memory row has length seven and both initial result words 99.
